question: Which option shows the correct answer when 27°C is converted to the kelvin scale?
solution:
The correct answer is __300 K.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kelvin (K)__ is the SI unit of temperature.
 
• To convert Celsius to Kelvin, use the formula: K = °C + 273.
 
• For 27°C: K = 27 + 273 = 300 K.
 
• Kelvin scale is absolute and starts from absolute zero, where molecular motion stops.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Absolute Zero:**

 
 
• Absolute zero is the lowest possible temperature where nothing could be colder.
 
• It is 0 K, equivalent to -273.15°C.
 
 
 
• **Celsius Scale:**
 
 
• The Celsius scale is commonly used in daily life.
 
• Water freezes at 0°C and boils at 100°C under standard conditions.
 
 
 
• **Fahrenheit Scale:**
 
 
• The Fahrenheit scale is used primarily in the United States.
 
• Water freezes at 32°F and boils at 212°F.
